paper.title: Bridging Rested and Restless Bandits with Graph-Triggering: Rising and Rotting

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic Rising GTBs with Block-Diagonal CMs
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution: pulling arm i advances the reward functions of all arms connected to i in a symmetric connectivity matrix G (interpolates rested and restless)
Connectivity matrix G is block-diagonal (disjoint union of cliques) and known to the learner
Rising: expected rewards non-decreasing and concave in the number of triggers, in [0,1]
Regret is policy regret against the optimal (clairvoyant) adaptive policy
settings.definition_quote: In this part, we propose two novel algorithms to learn in \emph{deterministic} Rising GTBs, \ie all instances of Rising GTBs where $\sigma=0$.

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic Rising GTBs with General Matrices
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution with a general symmetric connectivity matrix G, known to the learner
Rising: non-decreasing concave expected rewards in [0,1]
Policy regret against optimal adaptive policy
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T)$ be an instance of Rising GTB, where $\mathbf{G} \in \{0,1\}^{k\times k}$ and $\sigma=0$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Rising GTBs with Block-Diagonal CMs
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution with block-diagonal connectivity matrix G (unknown to the algorithm)
Rising: non-decreasing concave expected rewards in [0,1]; sigma^2-subgaussian noise
Policy regret against optimal adaptive policy
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T)$ be an instance of Rising GTB, where $\mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{B}_{\widetilde{k}}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Rising GTBs with General Matrices
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution with general symmetric connectivity matrix G (unknown to the algorithm)
Rising: non-decreasing concave expected rewards in [0,1]; sigma^2-subgaussian noise
Policy regret against optimal adaptive policy
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T)$ be an instance of Rising GTB, where $\mathbf{G}\in \{0,1\}^{k\times k}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Rotting GTBs with Block-Diagonal CMs
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution with block-diagonal connectivity matrix G (unknown to the algorithm)
Rotting: non-increasing expected rewards in [0,1] as a function of the number of triggers; sigma^2-subgaussian noise
Policy regret against optimal adaptive policy
settings.definition_quote: Let $(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T)$ be an instance of the Rotting GTBs, where $\mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{B}_{\widetilde{k}}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Rotting GTBs with General Matrices (lower bound)
unmapped: Graph-triggered evolution with a fixed non-block-diagonal symmetric connectivity matrix G (lower bound holds for any such G)
Rotting: non-increasing expected rewards in [0,1]
Lower bound built on deterministic instances (sigma = 0)
Policy regret against optimal adaptive policy

symbols.q: trade-off exponent in [0,1] (bound holds for the infimum over q)
symbols.Sum_A: sum over cliques C_m of |C_m| * Upsilon_nu(ceil(N_Cm/|C_m|), q), where Upsilon_nu(M,q)=sum_{t<M} max_i gamma_i(t)^q is the total increment and N_Cm the number of triggers of clique C_m by T
symbols.Sum_B: sum over cliques C_m of |C_m| * N_Cm^(q/(1+q)) * Upsilon_nu(ceil(N_Cm/|C_m|), q)^(1/(1+q))

conditions: Rising assumption: non-decreasing and concave expected rewards in [0,1]

results.notes: Regret is policy regret J* - J(pi) defined through expected rewards; mapped to pseudo_regret with comparator best_policy (optimal adaptive clairvoyant policy). Deterministic, so expectation is trivial. Algorithm described as anytime. Graph-dependent sums declared as symbols.

symbols.Sum_A_L: sum over cliques C_m^L of a maximal block sub-matrix of G of |C_m^L| * Upsilon_nu(ceil(N_{C_m^L}/|C_m^L|), q)
symbols.Sum_B_L: sum over cliques C_m^L of |C_m^L| * N_{C_m^L}^(q/(1+q)) * Upsilon_nu(ceil(N_{C_m^L}/|C_m^L|), q)^(1/(1+q))

conditions: Rising assumption: non-decreasing and concave expected rewards in [0,1]
tuning: uses a maximal block sub-matrix of G

results.notes: Computing the maximal sub-matrix is NP-hard (Remark 3, minimum clique partition), hence compute marked exponential; a heuristic sub-matrix gives a correspondingly scaled bound.

bound.expression_latex: \min_{q \in [0,1]} \{ (\sigma T)^{2/3} + \bar{k}_1 T^q \Upsilon_{\nu}(\lceil T/\bar{k}_1\rceil, q) + T^{\frac{2q}{1+q}} \sum_{C_m : |C_m| > 1} |C_m| \Upsilon_{\nu}(\lceil T/|C_m| \rceil, q)^{\frac{1}{1+q}} \}

symbols.Ups_k1: Upsilon_nu(ceil(T/k1bar), q), total increment sum_{t<M} max_i gamma_i(t)^q

Then, \algnamegenshort suffers an expected regret bounded by: ... where $\bar{k}_1$ is the number of cliques in $\mathbf{G}$ containing only one action.

results.notes: Proof gives an explicit bound with constants depending on eps, alpha, k (e.g. (3k/eps)(2 sigma T)^{2/3}(10 alpha log T)^{1/3}); the theorem states the O-tilde form, recorded here. Algorithm does not need G. Specialises to rested (G=I) and restless (G=1) known bounds.

symbols.Sum_C_U: sum over cliques C_m^U of the minimal block super-matrix of G of |C_m^U| * Upsilon_nu(T/|C_m^U|, q)^(1/(1+q))

source.label: thr:rottingregretLBgeneric
source.quote: For every $\mathbf{G} \in \{0,1\}^{k \times k}$ that is not block-diagonal, there exists an instance of Rotting GTB $(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T)$ such that, for every policy $\pi$, it holds: R_{\boldsymbol{\nu}, \mathbf{G}, T}(\pi) \geq \frac{T}{12}.

results.notes: Linear-regret (non-learnability) lower bound. The proof actually shows max over two deterministic instances is >= T/12, so the hard instance may depend on the policy; recorded as stated. Holds even when the learner knows G.
